page: Vultr vx1-g-8c-32g is a general-purpose virtual instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute line, providing dedicated hardware resources on the x86_64 architecture. The server is powered by an AMD EPYC processor delivering 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. Memory capacity is set at 32.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per thread. The processor integrates 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1 data cache, supported by advanced vector extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread compute capabilities alongside standard multi-core throughput. In synthetic CPU tests, the instance records top-tier performance in single-core stress-ng (3612.58) and single-threaded compression benchmarks, including 39.78 GB/sec in gzip and 17.59 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Text processing under Geekbench also places in the top decile. In contrast, multi-core throughput aligns with median performance profiles, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 7445.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 18506.84. Memory throughput achieves 72.12 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 41.41 GB/sec for writes.

A key operational tradeoff is local storage provisioning, as the instance includes only a minimal 1 GB local NVMe SSD, requiring external network block storage for stateful or data-heavy applications. Networking provisions include one complimentary public IPv4 address, and no hardware GPU accelerators are present. The balanced compute-to-memory profile and strong single-core performance make the instance suitable for general web serving, software build pipelines, and memory caching layers such as Redis.
description: Vultr vx1-g-8c-32g is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM. This provides a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include 32 MB of L3 cache, hardware AVX-512 extensions, one complimentary public IPv4 address, and a minimal 1 GB local NVMe SSD. Single-threaded performance benchmarks demonstrate high efficiency, scoring in the top tier for single-core stress-ng tests, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression. Multithreaded synthetic metrics align within standard median expectations. Because local NVMe storage is nominal at 1 GB, persistent file systems rely on attached network volumes. The configuration is suited for general application hosting, build systems, web serving, and in-memory caches.
